title: Character Generator Portrait or AI Generated Portraits?

posts.author: Darkmoon9
posts.body:
Hi, I have been rather divided on this issue for a while when it comes to my next game, Chronicles of Avineria. For my first game, Dextera Mortis, I commissioned a significant amount of art for the faces of characters in the game. The result was great, although a bit inconsistent when it comes to the art style because I employed more than one artist with different styles. But there was a major problem, doing this set me back more than a 2000 dollars. I just can't afford to keep bleeding money like that, especially not when I release my games for free, not if I want to continue to be able to create games. So continuing to commissioning art is simply not viable in the long run as long as I don't make any money from developing games. I have also grown really weary of scammers that I commisioned to make artwork who just sold me ai generated art instead.
So like leaves me with two alternatives, I either continue to use the ai generated assets for face portraits thats in the game right now, or I go back to using the RPG Maker MZ Chracterer Generator for face portraits. I am not interested in any debates about the ethicalility of AI. But if it is something that would drive away most of the playerbase, it might make it more of a risk than it is worth. I am also not entirely sure of the quality of the ai portraits, some of them look really good, others I am not sure about. Same with the generator portraits,some does capture the character, but others do not due to a lack of fitting generator parts. The ai images almost always capture the characters, at the cost of the type of small imperfections you almost always see with ai The question is, as a free option, what choice would render a higher quality experience?
I am currently leaning towards making two versions of the game, one with the ai generated images and one without. So people who don't like ai have a choice to play a version without them if they prefer. I just hope that would be enough to counter any negative impact on downloads that might come from using ai-
I also been thinking of creating a kickstarter to fund commisioned art. But I doubt that will get off the ground. Here is some screenshots with both ai portraits and the MZ character generator portraits. Which ones look best? I kinda want to gauge what the community thinks is the best way to proceed. Ai have also provided the ai version of the two Princesses of Licorne, Nyx and Dawn, as well as the Character Generator portraits for the same characters.
I guess another question is, should I even care if people have a problem with me using ai? Its for a game I release for free anyway. I also wonder if the general public even cares, or if its just a vocal minority. Its also possible that in the probably years this game will take to finish, the controversy would have long died out.
I have no plans of using ai in any other respects, just for the face graphics.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
First, you should use the internal face generator pictures as placeholders for as long as possible - you don't know how your game might change, perhaps even change some actors due to changes in the story.
Second, an average of 140$ for portraits is ... excessive, no other words for it.
I have commissioned hundreds of pictures for a different project over two decades, and while the last one was a decade ago (so prices will have substantially increased since then) that was still only 50$ for a full character picture in printable quality.
and RM-Games are mostly pixel art, which means a lot less dpi needed.
Yes, it sometimes takes a while to find an artist if you are on a budget, but if you for example check the classifieds offers here on this forum they are usually much cheaper than that
Third, an alternative that you might consider is to pay for a different character generator.
There are several independent character generators available on steam or on other sites, and this would get you a higher quality or at least different style of face pictures for less than one of your original commission prices.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Darkmoon9 said:
What does RTB stand for anyway?
Click to expand...
RTP*
Stands for Runtime Package and is kind of an old remnant name from back in the day when the default assets were a separate download. (Many elden peeps here will remember having to download the RTP to play most of the games made back in the day unless the developer included it when deploying.)
I commission Low personally for my characters, but he's also got loads of foes and other packs available on itch. I only really use the 8D gen for npc sprites and nothing else. I prefer the more detailed battlers from the commissions/packs.
You might also wanna consider just reusing the art assets you already have. Your new game can always feature the same characters and whatnot. You can make up any reason as to why or where on the timeline the new game takes place instead of constantly looking for new stuff.
Personally I just commission art and code. I'm by now means wealthy, but artists are slow and even I manage to save like 50 bucks a month so I can commission the stuff I need for my game. It's gonna take years anyway and you don't need to get everything at once either.
Outside of that, if you make free games, potentially only hosted on itch, you'll likely never get a big release anyway. So why worry about all that stuff? Why not just use the default + free stuff you can find to create interesting stories/mechanics? Why does it have to be custom or AI? Like whenever someone just says "I can't draw and I got no money" so they wanna use AI it just sounds like a shortcut.
If you can't do something and you can't afford it either, you can't have it. And drawing is literally free to get into. Especially digital. So that's kinda my main gripe I have with people using AI art. It always just boils down to "Buuuut I don' wanna doooo it!"

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Your peers (e.g. this forum or other indie game devs) will care a lot more about AI usage than core gamers and even more so casuals. It's not hard to imagine why artists and creators would be more against AI than consumers. AI has killed artist communities through sheer volume of output. Human creators simply cannot keep up with an endless deluge of generated content. This does affect consumers too if human creators are drowned out or drop out. AI content will be the only type left to consume, or the overwhelming majority of options available to consumers to consume.
If your game is only getting 78 downloads and free you should not be spending thousands of dollars on custom art. It's not sustainable, unless you're happy just being a wealthy patron. I personally would recommend cheap/free asset packs and editing/kitbashing them to make them your own.

Well, you are assuming I care about financial success, sustainability isn't the point. Its to accomplish my vision for the project.
My first game, Dextera Mortis, started out as a novel, the first version I wrote as a teen, and I have been developing the world and characters ever since. This story means alot to me. When it comes to characters I have a very specific vision in mind. They have had descriptions for a long time after all. Can't use any old assets, they actually have to match.
This game was the only version of this story I have finished to date. I.am just glad I put some version of it out there.
Even if it will probably never make a penny, this story is my legacy and I want to capture this vision as much as I could. The point of art is not to make money or become famous. It is to express yourself and your ideas. I just wish more people remembered that. After all, I hope when I am gone, my creations will remain, however small the audience.

If you do art for the sake of self expression, ai can ever replace you. If you like do create, do so. That should be the entire point.

If you're not concerned about ethics and stuff, I think that @Indinera said the games he publishes (at least on STEAM) from several developers that were filled with AI art sold better than "traditional" ones.
Click to expand...
The AI content of their games is almost always character art (and the subsequent capsule art since it includes one or several characters).
Sometimes they also use monsters packs that were made with AI and distributed on itch.
As those games rely heavily on storyline, AI tend to give them a fresher and more beautiful look. They are small games though, which aren't candidates for fame and glory. They just cater to their niche.
The problem with AI is that it will invade and overwhelm everything. But it's probably unstoppable at this point. Your best shot might be to make the most original game possible, and I'm obviously not talking about solely visuals. Plot, characters and gameplay matter too.

posts.author: Bobson
posts.body:
Just my two cents to weigh in.
First cent: If you're going the non-AI route, you can try looking for artist communities or sprite artists in legitimate place like here (I believe there are some) or other game development forums. If not, you can probably escrow the commission (or include a non-AI clause in a contract as someone suggested) so the funds are only released after verifying the art was not AI generated. Alternatively, instead of portraits, you can probably commission someone to make a portrait asset pack for the character generator.
Second cent: For me, AI is something like an alternative. I don't have any artistic talent and I estimate that I'll need years to learn the things needed to produce A-grade artwork. What I do have is imagination and the determination to learn. So I'll temporarily rely on AI art if needed (RMMZ + Free Assets first) while I try learning to make artwork on my own. Some people may not like it, but it's something I have already decided if I am to pursue my goals of making games.
By the way, my avatar is AI generated. It was B&W at first then I prompted a recolor with specific color palettes describing each part of the image. The concept description and specifics in my mind made the image possible then AI filled in the skill gap for me. Can't say it's better than actual artists, but it's something I can work with in the meantime. Ethics-wise, I'm not even sure if this is unethical, I'm not bothering any artist, I'm not 'stealing' art from anybody else, I don't think I'm cheating anyone. I'm just using AI to fill-in the lack in skill and realize what I imagine my characters would look like. Isn't that why technology exists?

posts.body:
So. Disclaimer. I voted to use the MZ generator images. That's my actual contribution to the thread. But I just had to comment on something:
rpgLord69 said:
Like I said, I don't have that strong a reaction about AI, but why are many heavy AI users so defensive always? Like you can say "of course it's a manner of thieving when people's data was harvested without consent" and just continue using AI anyway, right?
Click to expand...
If I had to guess, the severe reaction a lot of pro-AI users have isn't based on logic.
They finally get something that makes them feel validated or even worth something due to how it can express something for them they couldn't before (whether it's code, or art or whatever), without the conflicting personalities that go into interacting with real humans... only for huge and loud groups of people telling them they are morally/ethically/whatever type of wrong for using it.
Regardless of what the tool actually IS and the issues that come packaged with it, I can understand why the emotional disconnect is happening.
That's really all I can say because
at minimum
, I'm very much against using AI for actual projects and this thread is already becoming a bit of a Chernobyl for something that was supposed to be a simple query for what assets to use for a project.
Like for me when I design my characters, I use Gaia Online avatars to workshop what my characters look like because I'm a weirdo who can't draw - and then I pass them to my artists so they can turn those characters into real game art.

posts.author: Lord Vectra
posts.body:
I'll chime in late to the party. There are people who care and people who don't care. You're going to get a skewed perspective here since you're in a Game Dev blog. Some are going to hate me for saying this but its the truth:
If you plan to publish your game elsewhere other than here (i.e. Steam), if your game is good and as long as the AI art doesn't look horrid, majority of players won't care. That's just a fact, and we see games that admitted to using AI that is still successful. People here might not like it, but they can't deny it either.
So if you're asking this to test out the market, you will always lose customers if any spec of a game is AI regardless, so it comes down to if you care or if you think you'll lose enough to matter.
As for the poll, my answer isnt up there which is "I don't care."

Its kinda a moot point now anyway. The entire poll is is kinda moot. Did decide to go with solution: Non of the above, edit premade assets.
The main reason I created this thread in the first place was that I wasn't quite pleased with either the ai or character generator portraits. But still wanted to avoid spending 1000 dollars + on another project for art commissions. On my last project I spent more on that than every other asset combined. Buying asset packs for 25 dollars here and there is no issue. But 140 per image was a bit much for sustainability. This issue is solved, found a way to get portraits without ai that blows the ai images out of the water in my opinion.
The ai option no longer has the edge when it comes to presentation, which was the main argument for it in the first place. Granted, I am a pretty  prompter, have seen some people do things with AI that I can't.
And yes, one reason for the thread was also to gauge how many people people do have an issue with ai being used. Granted, the sample group might be a bit skewed. Wish I could poll the entire gaming community on it. But the facts remain is that this project is unlikely to hit the mainstream. So my player base are most likely mostly people in this community. There is no sense in shooting yourself in the foot when your demographic is already limited.
But at the end the day. The edited portraits look better than the ai portraits in my opinion, that above all is the deciding factor for me. That and not having to deal with the ai stigma is also a boon.
